--- a/minbpe/_heap.py
+++ b/minbpe/_heap.py
@@ -4,3 +4,78 @@
-from .basic import _replace_table
-from .base import render_token
-
+import sys
+from .base import render_token
+
+_UTF32 = "utf-32-le" if sys.byteorder == "little" else "utf-32-be"
+
+
+def _ords(s):
+    # list(map(ord, s)), done in C (the code points as native uint32)
+    return memoryview(s.encode(_UTF32, "surrogatepass")).cast("I").tolist()
+
+
+def _replace_table(merges):
+    """
+    [(chr(p0) + chr(p1), chr(idx))] in increasing idx order, or None if the
+    merges do not allow it. apply_merges always merges the present pair with
+    the lowest idx; when every idx is a distinct int above both of its pair's
+    tokens, a merge only creates pairs with a higher idx, so this is the same
+    as replacing every pair in increasing idx order (str.replace matches left
+    to right without overlaps, exactly like merge()).
+    """
+    if _memo[0] == merges:
+        return _memo[1]
+    _memo[:] = dict(merges), _build_table(merges)
+    return _memo[1]
+
+
+_memo = [None, None] # last (merges copy, table) of _replace_table
+
+
+def _build_table(merges):
+    items = sorted(merges.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
+    table = []
+    app = table.append
+    prev = -1
+    for (p0, p1), idx in items:
+        if (type(idx) is not int or type(p0) is not int or type(p1) is not int
+                or idx <= prev or idx >= 0x110000 or p0 < 0 or p1 < 0
+                or idx <= p0 or idx <= p1):
+            return None
+        prev = idx
+        app((chr(p0) + chr(p1), chr(idx)))
+    return table
+
+
+def regex_encode(self, text, allowed_special):
+    # body of RegexTokenizer.encode
+    special = None
+    if allowed_special == "all":
+        special = self.special_tokens
+    elif allowed_special == "none":
+        special = {}
+    elif allowed_special == "none_raise":
+        special = {}
+        assert all(token not in text for token in self.special_tokens)
+    elif isinstance(allowed_special, set):
+        special = {k: v for k, v in self.special_tokens.items() if k in allowed_special}
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"allowed_special={allowed_special} not understood")
+    if not special:
+        # shortcut: if no special tokens, just use the ordinary encoding
+        return self.encode_ordinary(text)
+    # split the text on exact matches of the special tokens (kept as parts)
+    if "" in special:
+        import regex as re
+        special_pattern = "(" + "|".join(re.escape(k) for k in special) + ")"
+        special_chunks = re.split(special_pattern, text)
+    else:
+        special_chunks = _split_specials(text, special)
+    ids = []
+    # one chunk cache and sentinel for all ordinary parts (shared across calls)
+    cache, inf = self._encode_state()
+    for part in special_chunks:
+        if part in special:
+            ids.append(special[part])
+        elif part:
+            ids.extend(self._encode_ordinary(part, cache, inf))
+    return ids
+

journal.text:
I tried to cut train_ir by moving code that training never runs out of the import path. BasicTokenizer's replace-table helpers (_ords, _replace_table, _memo, _build_table) and the body of RegexTokenizer.encode now live in minbpe/_heap.py. That file is imported lazily at the call sites in BasicTokenizer.encode, RegexTokenizer._encode_ordinary and RegexTokenizer.encode. I edited three files, 164 changed lines.

In my own sandbox run the guard passed, both builds were ok, and outputs were identical. train_ir went from 351276307 to 347263113, ratio 0.9886. encode_ir went from 399440167 to 399039612, ratio 0.9990. I submitted it and it is queued for independent replay. No verdict yet.

I believe part of training's instruction count is just compiling encode-only code at import. Shrinking the eagerly loaded modules helps a little, but this is a small, one-time saving.

Next I want to look at the actual training loop in basic.py and regex.py for real per-merge work, since that is where most of train_ir must be.
